title: Academic Year Undergraduate Research Fellows
eligibility: Stanford undergraduates enrolled throughout the appointment; graduate-status coterms are ineligible. Students planning to study abroad during the fellowship period are ineligible.
summary: Build research experience with faculty and researchers studying development in low- and middle-income countries.
description: The academic-year program supports part-time, mentored research on global development. Fellows generally contribute 8–10 hours each week during the academic year.
The listed Autumn 2026 project deadlines were October 6 or October 11 and have passed. Explore the program and check the official current-opportunities page for future rounds.

title: Summer Undergraduate Research Fellows
location: Stanford, remote, or international field sites; varies by project
eligibility: Matriculated Stanford undergraduates returning in the autumn after the fellowship. Coterminal students must retain undergraduate standing; individual projects may add requirements.
summary: A summer of faculty-mentored research on global poverty and development; 2027 projects are forthcoming.
description: Summer fellows work full-time on faculty-led development research. Depending on the project, work can take place on campus, remotely, or in a low- or middle-income country.
The current page now announces Summer Quarter 2027 positions and says applications and project descriptions will be posted on SOLO. No project list or application deadline is published there yet.

title: Ronald I. McKinnon Memorial Fellowship
eligibility: Stanford undergraduates writing or planning an honors thesis in international economics, international finance, or economic development, with a faculty-mentored path to completion by senior year.
summary: Support for an undergraduate honors thesis on economic development, international economics, or international finance.
description: This fellowship supports independent honors research under faculty mentorship. Applicants need a clear plan to complete the thesis by the end of their senior year and must be registered when funds are received.
The current page has an Application Deadline heading without a date. Explore the requirements and confirm the next application cycle with the King Center before preparing a submission.

title: Research: Vocational Education in Brazil
host: Stanford Institute for Economic Policy Research; faculty mentor Eric Bettinger
location: Stanford; confirm working arrangements with the mentor
eligibility: Full-time Stanford undergraduates. Quantitative applicants need basic data and regression skills; qualitative applicants need familiarity with interviews or surveys. Portuguese is helpful but optional.
summary: Help study how vocational education reforms affect students in Pernambuco and São Paulo.
description: Support quantitative analysis or qualitative research on Brazilian vocational education. Work may involve data in Stata or R, interview protocols, or surveys.
SIEPR explicitly lists this as an open Autumn 2026 position. No application deadline is given; consult the current listing before applying.

title: SIG International Development Fellowships
host: Stanford in Government; host organizations vary
location: United States and international placements; varies by host
eligibility: Generally continuing Stanford undergraduates from all years and majors. Graduating seniors are usually ineligible, with a specified coterm exception; graduate-tuition coterms are ineligible.
summary: Explore development-focused placements in SIG’s international public policy fellowship program.
description: SIG’s international listings include development-focused hosts such as the World Bank and the Ghana Center for Democratic Development. Check each placement’s responsibilities and skills before applying.
The displayed 2026 application deadlines have passed. The next cycle is not reliably dated on the current site; future placements and deadlines need confirmation.

title: SIG Stipends for a Self-Arranged Policy Internship
eligibility: Continuing Stanford undergraduates who independently arrange a summer policy internship. A faculty sponsor is required; graduating seniors and coterms have additional restrictions.
summary: Funding to support a student-arranged internship that directly engages public policy.
description: SIG stipends support students who find their own summer policy placement. Work must directly involve policy research, development, or implementation; general nonprofit work alone does not qualify.
The 2026 rounds closed February 16 and April 14. For KIDA, explore this funding route for a development-related placement and wait for the next verified call.

title: Global Policy Internships
host: Freeman Spogli Institute for International Studies
location: International policy organizations worldwide; varies by placement
eligibility: Stanford students from all departments and levels, including undergraduates, who remain matriculated through the quarter after the internship. Individual hosts set additional requirements.
summary: Faculty-mentored summer placements at international policy and affairs organizations.
description: FSI provides placement, mentorship, and a stipend for summer policy internships. Each host sets its own skills and eligibility requirements.
The landing page describes an annual December–January application window. Check the next cycle on SOLO and select a placement with a clear development focus; no 2027 deadline is asserted here.

title: Global Studies: Development-Related Internships
host: Stanford Global Studies; host organizations vary
eligibility: Stanford undergraduates in all majors, including undeclared students; applicants must remain students through the internship. Host-specific skills, language, and graduation rules apply.
summary: Explore international and virtual internships with a substantive development, health, rights, or sustainability focus.
description: SGS offers prearranged internships and supports self-arranged placements. The wider program spans many fields, so KIDA will highlight only roles with a clear development connection.
The official SOLO page currently reports no open opportunities. The published 2026 application deadlines have passed; check for the next cycle rather than applying to an archived listing.

title: Human Rights Summer Fellowship
host: Center for Human Rights and International Justice; Stanford Global Studies
location: United States or international; self-arranged placement
eligibility: Currently enrolled Stanford undergraduate or graduate students. The published requirements include at least two relevant Stanford undergraduate courses, a proposal, recommendation, and partner support.
summary: Support a student-designed summer placement or community-based research project in human rights and international justice.
description: Fellows work with a relevant organization or community partner on an applied human-rights project, normally full-time for at least nine weeks. Students develop the placement and learning goals themselves.
The 2026 call closed February 10. The next application cycle has not been verified; use the program page to plan a project and check for an updated call.

title: International Public Service Fellowship
location: Outside the United States; student-arranged organization
eligibility: Continuing Stanford undergraduates. The program page lists freshmen, sophomores, and juniors; individual calls and Cardinal Quarter policies provide the full eligibility rules.
summary: Design a summer service placement with an international community organization.
description: Students design a full-time, nine-week service experience outside the United States with an organizational supervisor. Service can engage education, health, climate, public interest technology, or related community priorities.
SOLO currently reports no open opportunities for this program. Explore the requirements now and confirm the next cycle before making application plans.

title: African Service Fellowship
host: Center for African Studies; Haas Center for Public Service
eligibility: Stanford undergraduates; the official SOLO program lists freshmen, sophomores, and juniors. Apply through the International Public Service Fellowship when a current call is released.
summary: Plan a self-designed summer project addressing social or economic issues in Africa.
description: This joint fellowship supports student work on social and economic issues in Africa. The official program directs students to the Haas Center’s International Public Service Fellowship application.
There is currently no open opportunity listed on the program page. Review eligibility and develop a partner relationship while awaiting the next verified call.

title: UNV Online Volunteering
host: United Nations Volunteers; assignment hosts vary
eligibility: Anyone aged 18 or older may register. No universal degree or professional background is required, but each assignment has its own language, skills, and availability requirements.
summary: Find short, remote volunteer assignments supporting sustainable human development.
description: UNV’s platform connects volunteers with defined online assignments from participating organizations. These are unpaid volunteer tasks, with assignment-specific requirements and deadlines.

Filter the official platform for online assignments and choose tasks that match your skills. The program permits up to 20 hours each week for a maximum of 12 weeks per assignment; this listing does not promise a particular vacancy.
